answer: Each challenge is bound to the identity's previous 4 answers, so the new answer must be consistent with them or be rejected at the haven check. Bindings are kept in bridge, verified in marble, and the chain is public. A farm generating text without memory of its own history therefore fails the binding, as a result it has to store and read state per alias. That bill is paid per identity, so 322 aliases cost 246 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
